Subject: KV cache / quant / routing sprint — onboarding checkpoints

Hi Ellen / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our chat, we want to make the onboarding for MedlyHealth focused and low-risk: a short sprint to stabilize cost and hit your latency targets before we expand traffic. Proposed scope for the initial 3-week workstream: 

- Week 0 (prep): collect traffic sample, slot-level SLAs, and any disallowed quantization/compliance constraints
- Week 1: enable KV prefix caching for stable prefixes, profile batching distribution, and run initial quantization candidates (int8/novel FP16 path)
- Week 2: routing rules and canary (latency vs cost tradeoff), fallback policies to larger models during spikes

Deliverables: checklist + runbook, a short spike report (latency & cost delta), and a rollout cadence for canary -> full.

Questions for you to confirm on our next call:
1) Which endpoints will carry production traffic week of launch (chat vs completion)?
2) Do you have an existing retention/SOC constraint around model weights or quant binaries?
3) Any blackout windows for canary traffic (payroll day, etc.)?

I attached a small traffic sample template — please drop your 48-hour sample (sanitized) and we’ll ingest it into the profiler.

Proposed next step: 40-minute kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT to align owners and handoff materials. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and map owner responsibilities.

Thanks,

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma

Hi Nikhil — thanks, this looks good and concise. A few notes from our side: 

- Primary traffic will be our triage assistant (chat-heavy flows) and a smaller completions-based summarization endpoint for internal ops. Expect 80/20 chat/completions.
- We can share a sanitized 72-hour sample (we prefer 72h to capture weekend traffic variability). I’ll attach it after today's security scrub.
- Compliance: we need to avoid shipping any third-party quant binaries into our VPC; if the quantized kernels are generated by Redwood but delivered as configuration (not binaries), that's OK. We can sign off after legal reviews.
- Blackout: we have a monthly billing reconciliation run on the 3rd of each month — plan to avoid heavy canaries around that day for the first rollout.

10am PT tomorrow works for us. Can Marissa from your side be the CS owner? She’ll be the day-to-day contact for runbook questions.

Thanks,

Marissa / team —

Quick technical clarifications so we scope the spike correctly: 

1) KV caching: what prefix characteristics should we prioritize? (stable user prompts, system prompts, or path-based prefixes). My suggestion: start with system prompts then expand to the top 20 frequent user prefixes after the first 48h of profiling.
2) Quantization: Medly requested config-only profiles. We can support this by generating quant tables in our build pipeline and exposing a profile id that can be toggled at runtime. That avoids shipping native kernels. Caveat: some micro-kernel improvements still require optimized libs; we should document performance deltas for profile-only toggles vs native builds. 
3) Routing: propose two routing policies for the canary: (a) cost-priority: route 30% traffic to cheaper int8-ish profile, (b) latency-priority: route 10% to larger FP16 baseline to keep tail latency SLAs. Canary can ramp 10 -> 30% over 2 hours if metrics stable.

I’ll bring numbers to the kickoff (expected throughput delta and token-cost delta for each profile).

-Karthik

Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
